subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth profile in main agentDir does not propagate to subagent sessions — silent fallback hallucinates tool calls in production

question: For spawned subagent runs that lose the selected Codex/OpenAI OAuth route, should OpenClaw fail closed, visibly warn and continue fallback, or keep the current fallback behavior after source-level OAuth inheritance is proven?
rationale: The choice controls whether private scheduled/channel context may cross provider boundaries after an auth failure, and the repo policy treats fallback behavior and auth/provider routing as compatibility- and security-sensitive.

options.title: Require live proof and fail-closed policy
options.body: Keep this open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and define a fail-closed or visible-warning behavior for auth-route loss.

options.title: Split visibility work after proof
options.body: Close only the OAuth propagation part after live proof and open a narrower fallback-visibility issue for remaining operator notification behavior.

options.title: Accept logged fallback only
options.body: Maintain the existing log-only fallback behavior after source proof, accepting the privacy and operator-surprise tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Require live proof and fail-closed policy
recommendation.body: Keep this open until a live current-main subagent run proves OAuth inheritance and define a fail-closed or visible-warning behavior for auth-route loss.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent history across OpenAI provider identity, auth-profile storage, Codex bridge context, and subagent/session routing, making them the best available owner for the cross-surface policy call.
